name: Rex-Ignis
description: Rex-Ignis earns its name as the king of fire, a volcanic world locked in a state of perpetual geological fury that makes it one of the most geologically active bodies ever surveyed. Supervolcanic calderas dot the surface in chains that follow the planet's tectonic boundaries, each one capable of eruptions that reshape entire continents. Between the calderas, vast obsidian plateaus gleam like dark mirrors, their surfaces cracked by thermal stress into tessellated patterns that stretch to every horizon.

The atmosphere is a choking soup of sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide, and volcanic particulates that reduce visibility to meters during eruption cycles and paint the sky in shades of burnt orange and sickly yellow. Volcanic lightning crackles continuously through the ash clouds, illuminating the landscape in stroboscopic flashes that reveal a world in constant violent motion. The heat is relentless, radiating from the ground itself, turning every surface into a potential burn hazard even through insulated equipment.

Despite the hellish conditions, Rex-Ignis harbors life. Extremophile microbial colonies thrive in the sulfur crystal formations and along the edges of lava flows, metabolizing sulfur compounds and heavy metals with biochemistry unlike anything found on temperate worlds. These organisms have been evolving in isolation for billions of years, developing solutions to heat stress and chemical toxicity that have immediate applications in industrial biotechnology. The lava tubes provide relatively stable environments where microbial mats grow centimeters thick.

Mining operations focus on the obsidian plateaus during quiescent periods between eruption cycles, though the definition of quiescent on Rex-Ignis still involves ground temperatures exceeding 200 degrees Celsius. The rivers of molten copper that flow from specific volcanic vents represent a resource extraction opportunity found nowhere else, but the logistics of harvesting liquid metal on a world that actively tries to destroy everything on its surface make this a venture for only the most ambitious or desperate. Three automated mining stations have been consumed by lava flows in the past decade alone.
